questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Were you serving the beautiful princesses of great Ireland?

options.text: Were the beautiful princesses of great Ireland being served by you?
Were the beautiful princesses of great Ireland served by you?
Were the beautiful princesses of great Ireland been served by you?
Was the beautiful princesses of great Ireland being served by you?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Were the beautiful princesses of great Ireland being served by you?"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• This is an example of the **past continuous tense.**
 
• Rules for this type of conversion:
 
 
• Acti**ve: ****Was/Were + subject + Verb ing form + object ?**
 
• **Passive: Was/Were + object + being + V-III + by + Subject?**
 
 
 
• While comparing with the basic structure:
 
 
• you(subject)
 
• serve(verb)
 
• the beautiful princesses of great Ireland(object)
 
 

Hence the correct answer: *Were the beautiful princesses of great Ireland being served by you?*

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

Jennifer Lawrence will have finished the shooting of the hideous movie.

options.text: The shooting of the hideous movie will have being finished by Jennifer Lawrence
The shooting of the hideous movie will be finished by Jennifer Lawrence
The shooting of the hideous movie have been finished by Jennifer Lawrence
The shooting of the hideous movie will have been finished by Jennifer Lawrence

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"The shooting of the hideous movie will have been finished by Jennifer Lawrence"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• To form the passive voice, you need to use the verb be in the same tense as the active voice, followed by the past participle of the main verb.
 
• The active voice sentence is in the future perfect tense, which uses will have + past participle.
 
• Therefore, the passive voice sentence should use will have + been + past participle.
 
• This is an example of the future perfect tense.
 
• Rules for this type of conversion:
 
 
• Active: **Subject + will have been + V-III + Object**
 
• Passive: **Object + will / shall have been + V-III + by + Subject**
 
 
 
• While comparing with the basic structure:
 
 
• Jennifer Lawrence(subject)
 
• finish(verb)
 
• The shooting of the hideous movie(object)
 
 

Hence the correct answer: *The shooting of the hideous movie will have been finished by Jennifer Lawrence*

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. 

Karim is to kill the enormous black snake in the garden of his house.

options.text: The enormous black snake was to be killed by Karim in the garden of his house.
The enormous black snake has to be killed by Karim in the garden of his house.
The enormous black snake is being killed by Karim in the garden of his house.
The enormous black snake is to be killed by Karim in the garden of his house.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"The enormous black snake is to be killed by Karim in the garden of his house."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is an infinitive sentence.
 
• Let’s look at the basic structure for this kind of conversion:
 
 
• **Active: Subject + verb + object**
 
• **Passive: Object + "to be" verb + past participle + by + subject (optional).**
 
 
 
• Look at the following examples:
 
• Active- I am to finish this work. 
 
 
• **Passive**- This work is to be finished by me.
 
• **Active**- You are to write an essay.
 
• **Passive**- An essay is to be written by you.
 
 
 
• Let’s compare the given sentence with the basic structure:
 
 
• **Subject- **Karim
 
• **1st form of the Verb- kill**
 
• **3rd form of the verb- killed**
 
• **Object-** the enormous black snake
 
 

Hence, the correct answer: *The enormous black snake is to be killed by Karim in the garden of his house.*

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. 

Ravina must clean my stinky clothes as soon as possible.

options.text: My stinky clothes must be cleaned by Ravina as soon as possible.
My stinky clothes should be cleaned by Ravina as soon as possible.
My stinky clothes might be cleaned by Ravina as soon as possible.
My stinky clothes could be cleaned by Ravina as soon as possible.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"My stinky clothes must be cleaned by Ravina as soon as possible."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• The given sentence is a sentence with a **modal.**
 
• Let’s look at the basic structure for this kind of conversion:
 
• If there is any model in the sentence, the helping auxiliary will only be “be” 
 
• There will be no change in the model.
 
• Use the 3rd form of the verb
 
 
• **Active: Subject+ modal auxiliary + verb+ Object**
 
• **Passive: Object + model auxiliary + be +3rd form of the verb + Subject **
 
 
 
• Look at the following examples:
 
 
• **Active**- I will write a letter. 
 
• **Passive** A letter will be written by me.
 
• **Active**- You must write a book.
 
• **Passive**- A book must be written by you.
 
 
 
• Let’s compare the given sentence with the basic structure:
 
 
• **Subject- Ravina**
 
• **Modal- must**
 
• **Object- My stinky clothes**
 
• **3rd form of the verb- cleaned**
 
 

Hence, the correct answer: *My stinky clothes must be cleaned by Ravina as soon as possible.*

questions.question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence. 

Sunaina was fascinated by the brilliant movie of Leonardo.

options.text: The brilliant movie of Leonardo fascinates Sunaina.
The brilliant movie of Leonardo fascinated Sunaina.
The brilliant movie of Leonardo was fascinating Sunaina.
The brilliant movie of Leonardo were fascinated Sunaina.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"The brilliant movie of Leonardo fascinated Sunaina."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is in the past indefinite tense.
 
• Let’s look at the basic structure for this kind of conversion:
 
 
• Active: Subject + 2nd form of the verb + Object.
 
• Passive: Subject(Object of Active) + was / were + 3rd form of the verb + by + Object(Subject of Active)
 
 
 
• Look at the following examples:
 
 
• Active- We won the match. 
 
• Passive- The match was won by us.
 
• Active- I purchased a pen.
 
• Passive- A pen was purchased by me.
 
 
 
• Let’s compare the given sentence with the basic structure:
 
 
• Subject(Object of Active)- The brilliant movie of Leonardo
 
• 1st form of the Verb- fascinated
 
• 3rd form of the verb- fascinated
 
• Object(Subject of Active)- Sunaina
 
 

Hence, the correct answer: *The brilliant movie of Leonardo fascinated Sunaina *

questions.question:
**Select the correct active form of the given sentence. **

An encouraging speech has been given by the coach to the football players.

options.text: The coach was given a ferocious speech to the football players.
The coach had given a ferocious speech to the football players.
The coach have given a ferocious speech to the football players.
The coach has given an encouraging speech to the football players.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"The coach has given an encouraging speech to the football players."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is in **passive voice.**
 
• Let’s look at the basic structure for this kind of conversion:
 
 
• Active: Subject + have / has +3rd form of the verb + Object
 
• Passive: Subject(Object of Active) + have / has been + 3rd form of the verb + by + Object(Subject of active)
 
 
 
• Look at the following examples:
 
 
• Active- He has bought a helicopter. 
 
• Passive- A helicopter has been bought by him.
 
• Active- He has damaged the car.
 
• Passive- The car has been damaged by him.
 
 
 
• Let’s compare the given sentence with the basic structure:
 
 
• Subject(Object of Active)- A ferocious speech
 
• 3rd form of the verb- given
 
• Object(Subject of active)- the coach
 
 

Hence, the correct answer: *The coach has given an encouraging speech to the football players.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct active form of the sentence.**

The completely damaged car is being repaired by Twinkle.

options.text: Twinkle is repairing the completely damaged car.
Twinkle was repairing the completely damaged car.
Twinkle is repaired the completely damaged car.
Twinkle repairs the completely damaged car.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Twinkle is repairing the completely damaged car."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is in **passive voice.**
 
• Let’s look at the basic structure for this kind of conversion:
 
 
• Active: Subject + is / am / are + verb + ing + Object
 
• Passive: Subject(Object of active) + is / am / are + being + 3rd form of the verb + by + Object(Subject of Active)
 
 
 
• Look at the following examples:
 
 
• Active- We are playing cricket.
 
• Passive- Cricket is being played by us.
 
• Active- She is making spaghetti.
 
• Passive- Spaghetti is being made by her.
 
 
 
• Let’s compare the given sentence with the basic structure:
 
 
• Subject(Object of active)- **The completely damaged car**
 
• 1st form of the Verb- repair
 
• 3rd form of the verb- repairing
 
• Object(Subject of Active)- Twinkle
 
 

Hence, the correct answer: *Twinkle is repairing the completely damaged car.*

questions.question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence. 

The big-looking project had been completed by Paul Wesley.

options.text: Paul Wesley has completed the big-looking project.
Paul Wesley completed the big-looking project.
Paul Wesley have completed the big-looking project.
Paul Wesley had completed the big-looking project.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Paul had completed the big-looking project."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in the passive form. 
 
• Let’s look at the basic structure for this kind of conversion:
 
 
• Active: Subject + had + 3rd form of the verb + Object
 
• Passive: Subject(object of active) + had been + 3rd form of the verb + by + (Agent) Object(Subject of Active)
 
 
 
• Look at the following examples:
 
 
• Active- He had killed a dog. 
 
• Passive- A dog had been killed by him.
 
• Active- They had completed the project. 
 
• Passive- The project had been completed by them.
 
 
 
• Let’s compare the given sentence with the basic structure:
 
 
• Subject(object of active)- The big-looking project
 
• 3rd form of the verb- completed
 
• Object(Subject of Active)- Paul Wesley
 
 

**Hence, the correct answer:** Paul had completed the big-looking project.

questions.question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

Can this utterly ridiculous situation be controlled by the masterclass Bailey?

options.text: Can the masterclass Bailey control this utterly ridiculous situation?
Can the masterclass Bailey controlled this utterly ridiculous situation?
Can the masterclass Bailey will control this utterly ridiculous situation?
Could the masterclass Bailey control this utterly ridiculous situation?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Can the masterclass Bailey control this utterly ridiculous situation?"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• In this type of question, the sentence starts with the modal auxiliary verb
 
• Rules for this type of conversion:
 
 
• Active: Modal Auxiliary + Subject + 1st form of the verb + object 
 
• Passive: Modal Auxiliary + Object+ be + 3rd from of the verb + by + subject
 
 
 
• While comparing with the basic structure:
 
 
• ​the masterclass bailey(subject)
 
• control(verb)
 
• can(auxiliary verb)
 
• this utterly ridiculous situation (object)
 
 

Hence the correct answer: *Can the masterclass Bailey control this utterly ridiculous situation?*
